correctness.rationale: The four-mode normal form reduces the problem to one real fidelity parameter. In the only non-Gaussian cross occupation sector, the bridge operator is gauge-equivalent to twice the four-cube adjacency operator. Its zero eigenspace consists exactly of the six weight-two Walsh characters, giving kernel norm squared \(3/2\) and rejecting norm squared \(1/2\) for the endpoint sum. Orthogonality of occupation sectors then yields \(r_4=F_{\mathrm G}(1-F_{\mathrm G})/2\). The distance-threshold and repeated-round formulas follow by monotonicity on \(F_{\mathrm G}\in[1/2,1]\) and independence. The exact rational checker reproduces the finite kernel calculation.

value.rationale: Four modes are the first nontrivial positive-parity setting in which pure fermionic non-Gaussianity appears, and the Bell test is the central practical tester in the recent literature. Replacing a uniform lower bound by the exact, attained rejection curve gives a complete finite-size soundness law and an exact confidence-vs-round tradeoff. The result is structurally motivated by the canonical four-mode orbit geometry rather than by an arbitrary parameter slice.
